rounds.text: Suyog Telematics trades at an attractive P/E of 16.1x compared to the sector benchmark of 20.99x [E1, E6], while its EV/EBITDA of 8.12x also sits well below the sector benchmark of 12.2x [E11]. The underlying business fundamentals show robust compounding, with 10-year sales and profit growth standing at 17% and 18% respectively [E14, E18], alongside a 5-year compounded profit growth of 21% [E19] and a striking 54% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded significantly to 75% in March 2026—a 10 percentage point increase over three years—backed by fully cash-realized profits and positive institutional money flow [E30, E34, E44]. Valuation models underline this disconnect, as a reverse DCF indicates that the current share price only requires a modest 5.3% earnings growth, contrasting sharply with the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E47]. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -31 Cr in March 2026 alongside an increase in borrowings and working capital days [E36, E39, E62]. Nonetheless, the rules-based screen awards the stock a strong 87 out of 100 with a medium confidence BUY rating, driven by accelerating earnings and net profit surging 200% year-on-year [E63, E65, E67].

Despite headline valuation metrics, Suyog Telematics carries significant operational and cash-flow risks that undermine its bull case. Free cash flow has turned sharply negative to negative 31 Cr in March 2026 [E36], while total borrowings surged to 335 Cr from 213 Cr a year earlier [E39], and working capital days expanded severely from 67 days to 143 days [E62]. Furthermore, capital intensity is escalating with Capital Work in Progress jumping by 91.3% to 88 Cr [E40], which coincides with a low dividend yield of 0.21% [E4] and a low dividend payout of just 2.98% of profits over the last three years [E61]. From a momentum and risk perspective, the stock carries high annualised volatility of 53.5% [E54], a negative Sharpe ratio of negative 0.37 [E55], and a severe historical peak-to-trough drawdown of 72.0% [E53], alongside a negative one-year price return of 2 percent [E25]. Operationally, the company's five-year sales growth is flagged as poor at 9.68 percent [E60], and its yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are both rated as inconsistent over recent periods [E32, E33]. Conceded: [E45] and [E46], which point to an intrinsic value above the current market price under a discounted cash flow model.

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 16.1x versus a sector benchmark of 20.99x [E1, E6] and features a reverse DCF implying only 5.3% earnings growth [E47]. However, the bull's valuation argument ignores critical capital allocation failures and cash flow destruction. Free cash flow plunged to Rs -31 Cr in March 2026 [E36], driven by a ballooning of working capital days from 67.0 to 143 days [E62]. Furthermore, borrowings spiked to Rs 335 Cr from Rs 213 Cr a year earlier [E39], while capital work-in-progress surged 91.3% to Rs 88 Cr [E40], exposing the business to heavy funding risks despite the optical P/E discount. Although 10-year sales and profit growth appear solid at 17% and 18% [E14, E18], recent performance is sluggish, with 5-year sales growth flagged as poor at 9.68% [E60] and the 1-year share price return sitting at -2% [E25]. Operating margins are classified as inconsistent over the last two years [E32], and the dividend payout remains negligible at 2.98% of profits over the last three years [E61]. Finally, the stock carries severe historical risks including an annualized volatility of 53.5% [E54], a Sharpe ratio of -0.37 [E55], and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -72.0% [E53].
